references.article_title: Help center guide for end users
references.intentional_differences: Results show title and tags only; no type filters or community. Departments such as Account Review are named only in articles, which is how the Agent finds the transfer path.

references.article_title: Submitting and tracking requests in the help center Customer Portal
references.intentional_differences: Topic, account reference and first message instead of email, subject and description: the customer is bound by Infra, not by an email field. No attachments (outside the approved scope).

references.article_title: Using structured messages in Zendesk Chat
references.intentional_differences: Quick actions are computed from the case state and are the same whether a better offer exists; they never name an offer or a department. Free text is answered by a deterministic recognizer, not a person or a bot builder.

references.article_title: Using structured messages in Zendesk Chat
references.intentional_differences: An offer card shows terms, conditions and expiry, and acceptance takes two steps (summary, then confirm); a reply in the chat never accepts. The reference is a one-click button message.

references.article_title: Submitting and tracking requests in the help center Customer Portal
references.intentional_differences: Cases carry status and tier chips; no search, filter or organization tabs.

references.article_title: Submitting and tracking requests in the help center Customer Portal
references.intentional_differences: The case view adds the quick actions, offer cards and the identity form. Provider commitments, reports and the overdue flag have their own page, which has no Zendesk counterpart.

no_public_reference.note: Identity checks inside a logged-in issuer chat are not publicly documented. Described from public help articles instead, as the approved proposal states; the implemented form sends only ticked fields.

no_public_reference.workflow: W3 Retention offers and W4 commitments
no_public_reference.note: Retention offers and a provider's commitment records are not shown in public documentation; no screenshot is invented.
